# Compass Award-Film Cyclical Production Protocol v1

## Purpose

This protocol is mandatory context for any AI room entering Compass award-film or chapter-video work. Its purpose is to preserve solved production knowledge, prevent unnecessary infrastructure invention, and make each completed film the verified baseline for the next bounded cycle.

The production system is media-first, hash-bound, cinematic-floor-preserving, owner-gated, and repository-governed at mutation/publication boundaries.

## Governing cycle

`BASELINE + SOURCES → INSPECT → BOUNDED CONSTRUCTION → RENDER → TECHNICAL QC → CINEMATIC QC → OWNER INSPECTION → PUBLISH → FREEZE SUCCESSOR → NEXT FILM`

Equivalent operating form:

`SOURCE CUSTODY → INSPECT → EDIT/COMPOSITE → COMPARE TO CINEMATIC FLOOR → RENDER → QUALIFY → OWNER → PUBLISH → RECORD RECEIPT`

Do not replace this cycle with an infrastructure-building cycle unless a real unresolved capability gap is proven.

## Reuse-before-infrastructure law

Before creating any new carrier, transport, recovery mechanism, workflow, governance layer, registry extension, source-materializer, or execution substrate, inspect the existing AI-entry instructions, verified source/master records, hashes, receipts, construction records, preservation amendments, checklists, connected custody, and already-installed tools.

If an existing verified mechanism already solves the required problem, use it. Do not recreate, wrap, parallelize, or elevate it into a new prerequisite merely because a fresh room has not yet loaded the prior solution.

A room change is not evidence of a capability gap.

Conversation loss is not authority to reconstruct solved infrastructure from memory.

## Source custody priority

Use the simplest authoritative source that allows exact inspection and construction:

1. an already materialized or directly room-accessible authoritative asset;
2. a verified connected Drive, site-owned, local, or other established master/source occurrence;
3. repository media when directly accessible;
4. exact-byte Git/GitHub/remote recovery only when the authoritative asset cannot otherwise be inspected or materialized.

Transport route does not establish media identity. Exact identity is established by the governing hash and technical properties. A byte-identical asset with the expected SHA-256 is the same authoritative media object regardless of whether it arrived through Drive, a local workspace, site-owned custody, GitHub, or another approved carrier.

Do not rematerialize or re-transport an asset whose exact identity is already proven and whose bytes are accessible to the executing workspace.

## Baseline preservation law

For a successor film, the current approved/live master is a positive cinematic baseline, not disposable source material.

`SUCCESSOR = PRESERVED_BASELINE_FUNCTION + AUTHORIZED_STRENGTHENING`

Never:

`SUCCESSOR = EMPTY_TIMELINE + AVAILABLE_SHOTS`

Preserve successful narrative function, typography hierarchy, reading states, motion/stillness grammar, transitions, overlays, spatial continuity, audio continuity, and pacing unless a specific governed deficiency justifies a bounded change.

Newer footage is not automatically better footage. Replace only a demonstrated weakness and preserve the job performed by the interval being changed.

The Chapter 01 live-baseline comparison amendment and construction progress checklist remain authoritative cinematic/QC controls where applicable. They are not instructions to create additional infrastructure.

## Construction rule

Construction should occur in an authorized media workspace using verified baseline and source assets. A normal cycle should spend its effort on picture, sound, typography, transitions, proof, pacing, and narrative coherence—not on repeatedly proving that already-solved transport machinery exists.

Before changing an interval, record:

- what the baseline interval accomplishes;
- the exact deficiency being corrected;
- the authorized replacement/extension source;
- the successful function that must survive;
- the evidence that the successor is stronger in the complete traversal.

If no deficiency is identified, preserve the interval.

## Technical qualification

Every rendered master must be freshly qualified against its governing technical profile. At minimum verify duration/frame count as applicable, resolution, frame rate, codec/pixel/color profile, audio continuity/profile, decode integrity, and exact SHA-256. Additional chapter-specific technical gates remain controlling.

Technical validity does not establish cinematic quality.

## Cinematic qualification

Watch the complete candidate linearly before owner handoff. Compare it directly against the protected cinematic floor and current approved baseline.

Reject a candidate that technically passes but weakens traversal causality, reading-state authority, typography, color hierarchy, transitions, spatial continuity, signature visual language, proof clarity, pacing, or ending resolution.

Sampled frames are supporting evidence, not a substitute for full-film inspection.

## Owner boundary

A candidate that passes internal technical and cinematic qualification stops at owner inspection unless the active operation explicitly carries publication/replacement authority.

Do not replace a live master merely because a render exists or machine checks pass.

Owner approval is a distinct gate.

## Publication and governance boundary

Repository admission, exact-path governance, mutation controls, merge rules, deployment rules, and public fetchback remain mandatory when repository or live-state mutation is actually being performed.

They must not be misapplied as redundant prerequisites to ordinary pre-publication media inspection, editing, compositing, or rendering when exact source identity and construction authority are already established.

Govern the mutation boundary; do not turn governance into the creative-production engine.

## Recovery/transport escalation

Escalate to exact-byte Git/GitHub/remote recovery only after establishing that the authoritative asset is genuinely unavailable through simpler approved custody.

Before escalation, answer all of the following:

- Is the exact asset already accessible in the current room/workspace?
- Is a byte-identical master/source present in connected or established custody?
- Is its expected SHA-256 known and verifiable?
- Does an existing materializer/carrier already solve this exact case?

If any existing route supplies exact verified bytes, use it and continue construction.

Do not design a new transport system as a substitute for checking existing custody.

## Over-engineering stop rule

Do not add a new prerequisite, tool, carrier, workflow, registry layer, or governance object unless it materially improves at least one of:

- picture or sound quality;
- source truth or exact media identity;
- cinematic non-regression;
- technical qualification;
- publication integrity;
- safety or scope containment;
- durable handoff/recovery where no existing solution already provides it.

If an existing verified solution already handles the need, the proposed addition is unnecessary and must not block the film cycle.

Complexity is not evidence of rigor. The smallest verified mechanism that preserves authority and quality is preferred.

## Room recovery and continuation

A fresh room must first recover the current verified state rather than restart the cycle.

Read the AI entrypoint, this protocol, the governing chapter construction contract, the applicable baseline-preservation amendment/checklist, and the latest execution/qualification record. Continue from the first genuinely incomplete production gate.

Do not reopen solved gates because the executor changed rooms. Do not infer completion when evidence is absent.

## Required durable handoff after each film

Every completed cycle should leave enough evidence for another room to continue without reconstructing the conversation:

- exact approved master identity and SHA-256;
- baseline identity it succeeded;
- source manifest/identities and materialization status;
- edit/construction record or bounded delta ledger;
- technical qualification receipt;
- cinematic qualification/non-regression result;
- owner decision;
- publication/live identity when applicable;
- next lawful state.

The approved successor then becomes the comparison baseline for the next bounded cycle.

## Governing principle

Use what has already been solved. Verify exact identity. Improve only what is weak. Preserve what is strong. Render and inspect the whole film. Publish only through the governed boundary. Freeze the approved result and repeat.
